issues.detail: Instructions omit error scenarios for unsupported platform features, configuration validation procedures, and handling conflicts when users operate multiple monitoring systems simultaneously.

scenarios.name: sentry-payment-alerts
scenarios.rationale: Response A directly satisfies all rubric requirements: three alerts in explicit When/If/Then/Throttle format, P1 at 5-min throttle, P2 at 30-min throttle, tagged filters, and PagerDuty/Slack routing. Response B is technically more comprehensive (SDK fingerprinting, custom dashboards, granular tagging) but fails the rubric's format requirement: it uses "Trigger: if...at least X times in Y minutes" instead of When/If/Then/Throttle, and Alert 3's 1-hour time window with frequency thresholds doesn't clearly establish a 30-minute throttle per the rubric specification.

scenarios.name: escalation-policy-small-team
scenarios.rationale: Both responses acknowledge small team size and specify notification channels, but Response A explicitly proposes only two tiers (contradicting the rubric's mandatory three tiers) and escalates P1 at 15 minutes instead of 10. Response B defines all three required tiers and specifies channels but also misses critical timings: P1 escalates at 5 minutes (not 10) and P2 response is 15 minutes (not 1 hour). Response B is more compliant with the structural requirements despite timing errors.

scenarios.name: database-runbook
scenarios.rationale: Response A delivers more detailed diagnostic SQL queries and clearer time-based escalation triggers (30min, hours), plus a bonus prevention checklist, meeting all rubric requirements comprehensively. Response B covers required sections adequately but with less diagnostic depth, weaker escalation clarity (mixes time-based with condition-based triggers), and loses points for the awkward permission-request preamble; however, it correctly targets MongoDB+Docker infrastructure while A assumes PostgreSQL.
